newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wesfarmers shares soar to record high.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wesfarmers shares soar to record high.

text.p: Shares in Wesfarmers Ltd climbed 35 cents to a record high A$10.45 on Wednesday as investors bought in on a strong first half profit result and an upbeat outlook for the West Australian-based pastoral and energy house.
"There is a good feeling going around the market that the last result was very positive with better things to come in the next six months," said a Perth-based dealer.

On February 11, Wesfarmers reported a 50.5 percent higher net profit of A$57.55 million for the six months to December 31, 1996, and increased their interim dividend to 20 cents per share from 17 cnets per share.

In posting the stronger result, Wesfarmers cited higher contributions to group profits from the fertilisers and chemicals unit, Wesfarmers CSBP, and a big turnaround in rural and insurance unit, Wesfarmers Dalgety.
The company also said the outlook for its full financial year remained very favourable, despite subdued conditions in the housing industry, and the wool and livestock sectors of the rural industry.

"They have taken the pain of the bad results of 12 months ago and it looks pretty straight ahead from here. People are putting targets of A$11 to A$12 on the shares for the next six to twelve months," the dealer said.
Wesfarmers is about 51 percent owned by The Franked Income Fund whose units also reached a record high, up nine cents to A$3.10.
Wesfarmers shares closed at their A$10.45 high on turnover of 341,460 shares.
